title: Content Pillars Strategy
subtitle: You post content randomly, whatever feels relevant that day. Your audience doesn't know
useWhen: what to expect from you and your posts attract different people with no consistent theme. You have followers but no community.
howToUse: Content Pillars are the 3–5 core topics that define what you stand for online. Each pillar represents an area where your brand has genuine expertise and your audience has genuine interest. Every piece of content you create sits under one pillar. This creates consistency your audience knows what you're about and self-selects if they're the right fit. It also makes content creation faster instead of asking 'what should I post today?' you ask 'which pillar am I covering this week?'
steps: Choose pillars that sit at the intersection of your expertise and your audience's needs.
Each pillar should be specific enough to exclude broad pillars dilute positioning.
Allocate content across pillars by week not every post needs to be educational.

Review pillar performance every 90 days and retire any pillar that consistently underperforms. Post with purpose build an audience that trusts you Pillars Aren't Permanent Picking pillars once and never revisiting them is how brands go stale. What your audience needed a year ago isn't what they need now. The 90-day review isn't optional housekeeping it's how you catch a pillar that's coasting on habit instead of earning its place in your content.
origin: Content marketing best practice — content pillar methodology, widely adopted 2015s onwards

Step 3     :  Suggest one signature content format I should own,

proTip:
Your signature content format is more valuable than your best single post. A consistent
format, a weekly framework breakdown, a Monday mindset post, a Friday lessons-
learned thread - trains your audience to expect and look for you. Consistency of format
compounds faster than variety of topics.
